Package dyntabs.ai.voice

Class Speech

java.lang.Object
dyntabs.ai.voice.Speech
public final class Speech extends Object
One piece of synthesized audio: the bytes plus the MIME type needed to serve them.

Why both halves travel together

A bare byte[] is not enough to answer an HTTP request: the caller must also set a Content-Type, and guessing it is how audio ends up silently unplayable in a browser. Keeping the two together means a web endpoint never has to invent the second half:


 Speech speech = EasyAI.speak().from("Order ORD-004 has been delivered.");
 return Response.ok(speech.bytes()).type(speech.mimeType()).build();

base64() is there for the other common destination — embedding the clip straight into a JSON reply or an HTML <audio src="data:..."> attribute.

Note on the array: bytes() hands back the internal array without copying. Audio clips are large enough that defensive copying on every call would be a real cost for a value nobody mutates in practice; treat it as read-only.

Analogy: a parcel with its shipping label already attached. The contents alone would get stuck at the depot — it is the label that tells the courier what to do with it.
